SAMUEL ACHTERBERG-OSEI
Cloud Engineer | Azure Infrastructure & DevOps
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating Azure infrastructure, building Terraform modules, and automating application releases with Azure DevOps. Recent work includes hub-and-spoke networking across three subscriptions, AKS operations, and deployment pipelines for internal applications. Background in systems administration, Windows and Linux servers, VMware, and PowerShell automation. Azure Administrator Associate certified; Terraform Associate certified in 2025.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure IaaS, Azure Migrate, Terraform, Azure landing zones, Azure Firewall, Azure VNets, hub-and-spoke networking, VNet peering, private DNS zones, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN
Platform and delivery: Azure DevOps, YAML pipelines, Docker, AKS operations (upgrades, node pools, ingress), Helm, Azure App Service, CI/CD
Systems and automation: Windows, Linux, VMware, PowerShell, Proxmox, Python (small scripts), Go (Terratest tests)
Security: Microsoft 365, Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, backup checklists

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–Present
- Build and maintain Azure landing-zone infrastructure and Terraform modules.
- Created a hub-and-spoke network using Terraform, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across three subscriptions.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and implemented a nightly drift-detection job.
- Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Increased deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS, including upgrades, node pools, and ingress; application manifests are owned by developers.

Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023
- Developed a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for small-business Microsoft 365 security baselines, covering MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, and backups.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2014–2020
- Administered Windows and Linux servers and supported staff across several municipal services.
- Looked after an environment of around 250 Windows and Linux servers.
- Planned and executed the 2019 lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate.
- Completed cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Used Azure VMs, VNets, site-to-site VPN, and PowerShell as part of the migration and systems administration work.

CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

Career Break | Mar 2020–Aug 2022
- Left municipal employment to provide full-time care for his father, who passed away in 2022.
- Kept Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) knowledge current and provided unpaid IT help to church and family.

Freelance Work Gap and Professional Development | Feb 2024–Feb 2025
- Studied Terraform and built a Proxmox homelab.
- Completed a three-month, part-time, online English-language cloud bootcamp in December 2024.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Azure Landing Zone Networking | Havenstad Logistics | 2025
- Built hub-and-spoke Azure networking in Terraform across three subscriptions, with Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, and VNet peering.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and nightly drift detection.

Release Pipelines for Internal Apps | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–2026
- Automated build, test, and deployment for 15 internal .NET and Node applications using Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, Docker, AKS, Helm, and App Service.

VMware to Azure Migration | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2019
- Migrated 60 servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate, completing cut-over over six weekends without unplanned downtime.

Small-business Microsoft 365 Security Baseline | Freelance | 2022–2023
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, and backups.

CERTIFICATIONS
- Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate
- HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (2025)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear Azure infrastructure and DevOps profile. It contains credible technical detail, useful scale indicators, and measurable outcomes such as 15 automated applications, three Azure subscriptions, 60 migrated servers, approximately 250 administered servers, and increased deployment frequency. The progression from systems administration to cloud engineering is understandable, and the career breaks are explained professionally. The main content weaknesses are duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects, limited evidence of stakeholder leadership or formal system-design responsibilities, and a relatively broad technical-skills section that could be more tightly prioritized for this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, plain text structure, conventional date formats, and strong searchable terms including Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, YAML pipelines, AKS, Docker, Helm, Azure Firewall, VNets, private endpoints, VPN, Linux, VMware, PowerShell, and Azure Migrate. Its AI-screening probability is good for Azure infrastructure, Terraform, networking, and DevOps roles. Alignment will be weaker for this specific vacancy because the document does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, technical stakeholder leadership, or AWS. These are genuine candidate-profile gaps based on the supplied information, not merely keyword omissions. The duplicated project and employment descriptions may also dilute keyword relevance slightly, although they remain parseable.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure environment design and operation, Terraform-based networking, deployment automation, practical Microsoft 365 security work, Linux, and virtual-machine experience. The Azure landing-zone, hub-and-spoke, Azure Migrate, and AKS examples are relevant to a role involving production infrastructure and system reliability. It also shows operational ownership and collaboration with application developers through deployment pipelines. The candidate's material does not establish Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT or remote-device integration, AWS, JVM/backend development, or explicit experience leading technical proposals and bringing stakeholders along. The document should not imply those capabilities. The CV is therefore a strong transferable Azure match but not a complete match for the fleet-connectivity security and stakeholder-leadership scope.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence beginning “Background in systems administration” with a more role-targeted but truthful statement such as: “Brings systems-architecture and operations experience from Azure landing-zone design, hub-and-spoke networking, a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration, and operation of Windows and Linux environments.” This makes the systems-design relevance more explicit without claiming unsupported formal architecture ownership.

2. In the Professional Experience section under Havenstad Logistics, revise “Build and maintain Azure landing-zone infrastructure and Terraform modules” to “Design, build, and operate Azure landing-zone infrastructure and Terraform modules.” This uses the job description’s infrastructure-engineering language and is supported by the documented landing-zone and networking work.

3. In the Havenstad Logistics bullets, make the developer-facing collaboration explicit without overstating stakeholder leadership. Change the deployment bullet to: “Partnered with application developers to replace manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS.” Only use this wording if “partnered” accurately reflects the actual working relationship; otherwise retain the current wording.

4. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. Keep the detailed achievement bullets under each employer, and convert Selected Projects into a compact “Selected Infrastructure Projects” section with one concise line per project, or remove the repeated project section entirely. Preserve the strongest distinct facts: three-subscription hub-and-spoke networking, 15 applications, 60 migrated servers, and the no-unplanned-downtime result.

5. In the Technical Skills section, reorder the categories so the most relevant terms appear first: “Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, Terratest, Azure landing zones”; “Cloud and Networking: Microsoft Azure, Azure IaaS, Azure VNets, hub-and-spoke networking, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN”; “DevOps and Platforms: Azure DevOps, YAML pipelines, Docker, AKS, Helm, Azure App Service.” This improves prioritization for ATS and human reviewers without adding unsupported tools.

6. In the Career Breaks and Professional Development section, shorten the caregiving explanation to protect privacy and improve focus. For example, change “Left municipal employment to provide full-time care for his father, who passed away in 2022” to “Family caregiving leave.” Retain the supported professional-development details about maintaining AZ-104 knowledge and providing unpaid IT help if desired.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and appropriately focused on cloud infrastructure and DevOps. It provides strong evidence through concrete scope and outcomes, including three Azure subscriptions, 15 applications, 60 migrated servers, approximately 250 administered servers, and increased deployment frequency. The chronology is transparent and the career breaks are explained without creating unexplained gaps. The main content limitation is that the Selected Projects section substantially repeats the Professional Experience section, which increases length without adding much new evidence. The CV also does not explicitly demonstrate several role requirements such as technical leadership, stakeholder alignment, system design, or secure certificate-based communication.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The headings, conventional section order, plain text contact details, standard date formats, and bullet structure are ATS-friendly. The document includes strong searchable terms such as Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, YAML pipelines, AKS, Azure Firewall, VNet peering, private endpoints, Azure Migrate, PowerShell, Linux, VMware, CI/CD, and Docker. AI screening probability is reasonably high for Azure infrastructure, Terraform, DevOps, migration, and platform operations roles, but only moderate for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain supported evidence or terminology for Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, system design, technical leadership, stakeholder management, or AWS. The repeated project content may dilute keyword relevance slightly, but there are no major parsing or formatting problems.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure cloud environment design and operation, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, networking, practical security controls, Linux, and virtual machines. It also demonstrates relevant operational ownership through landing-zone work, AKS operations, deployment pipelines, drift detection, and migration execution. Azure is an acceptable major cloud for the advertisement, although AWS is preferred and the candidate's notes explicitly state there is no AWS experience. The candidate material does not establish Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, IoT or automotive integration, JVM development, formal system-design responsibility, or experience leading technical proposals and bringing stakeholders along. The CV also does not directly evidence strong analytical thinking and clear communication, although the quantified migration and automation outcomes provide indirect evidence. The transportation context is potentially relevant, but no fleet, vehicle, telemetry, remote-device, or train-to-cloud experience is documented.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES:
None identified. The CV's claims are supported by the Original Candidate Information and portfolio. Do not add AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT, automotive, JVM, or stakeholder-leadership claims unless the candidate can substantiate them.

MINOR / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the current summary with a tighter version that foregrounds the strongest matching evidence and uses supported job terminology: "Cloud engineer with hands-on experience designing, building, and operating Azure infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code with Terraform. Experience includes Azure landing zones, hub-and-spoke networking across three subscriptions, Azure DevOps CI/CD, AKS operations, Azure IaaS migration, and practical Microsoft 365 security automation. Azure Administrator Associate and Terraform Associate certified." This improves relevance without claiming unsupported system-design, Terragrunt, TLS, or leadership experience.
2. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Cloud and infrastructure" to "Cloud Infrastructure and Networking" and rename "Platform and delivery" to "DevOps and Platform Engineering." Keep the existing supported terms, including "infrastructure as code," "Azure landing zones," "hub-and-spoke networking," "Azure Firewall," "private endpoints," "site-to-site VPN," "CI/CD," and "AKS operations," to improve alignment with the advertisement.
3. In the Cloud Engineer experience section, revise the first bullet to make the infrastructure-engineering scope more explicit: "Design, build, and operate Azure landing-zone infrastructure and reusable Terraform modules." This uses the job's wording while remaining supported by the candidate information.
4. In the Cloud Engineer experience section, revise the AKS bullet to make the ownership boundary clearer and more credible: "Operate AKS clusters, including upgrades, node-pool management, and ingress; application manifests remain owned by development teams." The current wording is already truthful, but this version is more concise and ATS-readable.
5. In the Systems Administrator experience section, combine the two server-administration bullets to reduce repetition and increase impact: "Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting several municipal services, including VMware-based infrastructure and Azure VMs." Keep the separate migration bullet immediately after it because the 60-server scope and no-unplanned-downtime result are strong evidence.
6. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. Either remove the duplicated project bullets or shorten each project to a one-line technology-and-outcome entry. For example, retain the detailed evidence under Professional Experience and make the project entries: "Azure Landing Zone Networking — Terraform hub-and-spoke network across three subscriptions; Azure Firewall, private endpoints, private DNS, VNet peering, Terratest, and nightly drift detection." This preserves keywords while making the CV more concise.
7. In the Selected Projects section, change "Technologies"-style information into searchable inline terms within each project description, rather than repeating a separate project summary that duplicates the employment bullets. Prioritize Terraform, Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, AKS, Helm, App Service, Azure Migrate, PowerShell, Linux, VMware, and Azure networking because these are the strongest supported matches.
8. In the Career Breaks and Professional Development section, change "Left municipal employment to provide full-time care for his father, who passed away in 2022" to the more concise and professional "Career break for full-time family caregiving, Mar 2020–Aug 2022." Retain the information about maintaining AZ-104 knowledge and providing unpaid IT help, but avoid including a family member's cause-of-life detail unless specifically required.
